hints: Look first at electrical conductivity, as this is the fastest way to separate metals, ionic compounds and molecular substances.
Substance P conducts well even as a solid and gives an alkaline solution with water, which points to a reactive Group 1 metal like sodium or potassium.
Substance Q never conducts, has a very low melting point and gives an acidic solution, so link that to a non-metal oxide with weak forces between molecules.
walkthrough:
**Use conductivity to identify P**

Only one type of structure conducts electricity when solid. That is giant metallic, because delocalised electrons can move through the lattice even without melting.

Rule: conducts solid + molten = metallic. Conducts molten only = ionic. Never conducts = molecular or giant covalent.

**Check P with water and melting point**

P reacts vigorously to give an alkaline solution. That fits a reactive metal forming a metal hydroxide, for example:
$$2\text{Na} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2$$
Its melting point of 454 K is low for a giant structure, but typical for an alkali metal, not for giant ionic which is usually much higher.

**Use all clues to identify Q**

Q does not conduct in any state, so there are no mobile electrons or ions. Its melting point of 317 K is very low, so only weak intermolecular forces are broken on melting. That means simple molecular.

Its vigorous reaction to give an acidic solution fits an acidic non-metal oxide, for example:
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$

**Combine to choose the row**

P is giant metallic and Q is simple molecular. That combination matches the correct row.

options.A: Correct. P conducts as a solid so must be giant metallic, and alkaline reaction confirms a reactive metal. Q never conducts, has low melting point of 317 K and gives acidic solution, so must be simple molecular non-metal oxide.
options.B: Reversed logic. Simple molecular substances never conduct because they have no free electrons or ions, so P cannot be simple molecular. Giant metallic substances always conduct as solids, so Q cannot be giant metallic.
options.C: Trap for ionic. Giant ionic conducts when molten but never when solid because ions are fixed in the lattice. Since P conducts well when solid, it cannot be ionic. Q as simple molecular is correct, but P is wrong.
options.D: Half correct. P as giant metallic is correct, but Q cannot be giant ionic. Giant ionic solids have very high melting points and conduct when molten, whereas Q has a very low melting point of 317 K and never conducts.
